text:
Unit Fifteen
Capitalization and Punctuation
Read the passage below:

subject: English_grammar
text:
Musa Ibrahim is the first Bangladeshi who reached the summit of Mount
Everest. Mt. Everest is the highest pick of the Himalayas. He had a dream
to win Mount Everest. To make his dream real he tried heart and soul. He
got Advanced Mountaineering Training from Himalayan Mountaineering
Institute, Darjeeling, India. He was a journalist by profession. He worked
as a sub editor in The Daily Star. He founded Everest Academy in 2011 for
a wide participation of the youth in the mountaineering and adventure
activities.

subject: English_grammar
text:
Note: The underlined words start with capital letters (upper case). Other
words begin with small letters (lower case). There are rules to use capital
letters in English. The use of capital letters is called capitalization.
Use of Capital letters:
e Asentence begins with a capital letter. For example:

subject: English_grammar
text:
We want to learn English capitalization rules.
These students are learning English as a foreign language.
The sky is cloudy.
e The first word of a quoted sentence begins with a capital letter.
Teacher said, “Always speak the truth.”
e Proper nouns begin with capital letters. (Names of people, specific
monuments, cities, states, etc.). For example:

subject: English_grammar
text:
Mr. Tarek asked if Ali would help.
Uncle Bill took us to Dallas.
English Grammar and Composition 131
e A person's title begins with a capital letter when it comes before his
or her name (Dr. Rehana)
e The position of high-ranking government officials begins with a
capital letter. (for example, President Bill Clinton, Attorney General

subject: English_grammar
text:
Shahed)
e The pronoun | is always capitalized whenever it is used. For
example:
| want to go to Sylhet.
My sister and I are in the same class.
e The first and any important word in the title of a book, magazine,
song, movie, poem, or any other work begins with a capital letter.
For example:
Read the first chapter of Gulliver’s Travels.
| saw American Pie last year.

D. Punctuation
Read the following passage:

subject: English_grammar
text:
Once a lion, a fox, and a wolf went hunting. They ultimately spotted a stag
and killed him for their food. While sharing the hunt, “Quarter me this stag”,
roared the lion and other animals skinned and cut the spoil into four equal
parts.
Note: In the passage there are some marks with the words. These marks
help us to understand the passage. These marks are the punctuation marks.

subject: English_grammar
text:
132 English Grammar and Composition
Punctuation Rules:
Apostrophe (')
Examples: 1. She can’t join the party. (cannot)
2. Hon’ble President (Honourable)
3. Girls’ school
4. This is Karim’s house.
Note: To indicate omission of letters and the genitive case of nouns (') is used.

subject: English_grammar
text:
‘Period’ or ‘full stop’
1. A complete sentence that makes a statement or command ends with a
period. In British English a period is called a ‘full stop’.
Today is my birthday.
Blow out the candle.
He went to Khulna last week.
2. Most abbreviations end with a period.
Dr. Smith lives on Creek Rd. near St. Mary's Hospital.
Question Mark (?)

subject: English_grammar
text:
1. A question ends with a question mark.
When is she coming?
Are you Pollobi Khisa?
Exclamation Point (!)
1. The exclamation point is used at the end of a sentence to indicate great
surprise. It is also used for emphasis when making a point (strong feeling /
excitement).
Be careful not to use the exclamation mark too often.

subject: English_grammar
text:
What a wonderful day it is!
That ride was fantastic!
| can't believe he is going to marry her!
English Grammar and Composition 133
Comma (,)
1. A comma separates things in a series (List of items):
| ate rice, vegetables, and fish.

subject: English_grammar
text:
| like reading, listening to music, taking long walks, and visiting my friends.
This is one of the most common uses of a comma. Notice that a comma is
included before the conjunction 'and' which comes before the final element
of a list.
. Acomma separates an interruption from the rest of the sentence:
Mr. Walker, our teacher, is very clever.

subject: English_grammar
text:
. A comma separates two independent clauses that are connected by a
conjunction such as ‘but’:
They wanted to purchase a new car, but their financial situation would not
allow it.
| would really enjoy seeing a film this evening, and I'd like to go out for a
walk.
. Acomma separates phrases (or clauses) from the principal clause:

subject: English_grammar
text:
In order to pass the exam, you need to study more.
Although he wanted to come, he wasn't able to attend the course.
. Acomma introduces a direct quote:
The boy said, "My father is often away during the week on business trips."
His doctor replied, "If you don't stop smoking, you run the risk of a heart
attack."
Colon (:)
1. A colon shows the reader that a list or explanation follows:

subject: English_grammar
text:
| will need the following items: scissors, paper, glue, and paint.
He had many reasons for joining the club: to get in shape, to make new
friends, to lose some weight, and to get out of the house.
134 English Grammar and Composition
2. To introduce a direct quote (a comma can also be used in this situation):

subject: English_grammar
text:
He announced to his friends: "I'm getting married!"
She cried out: "| never want to see you again!"
Semicolon (;)
There are two uses for a semicolon:
1. To separate two independent clauses. One or both of the clauses are short
and the ideas expressed are usually very similar.
He loves studying; he can't get enough of school.
What an incredible situation; it must make you nervous.

subject: English_grammar
text:
2. To separate groups of words which are themselves separated by commas:
| took a holiday and played golf, which | love; read a lot, which | needed to
do; and slept late; which | hadn't done for quite a while.
They plan to study German, for their travels; chemistry, for their work; and
literature, for their own enjoyment.

subject: English_grammar
text:
Warning: Do not use a capital letter after a semicolon, unless it is followed by
a proper noun.
Quotation Marks (double " or single ')
1. Quotation marks are used to identify the exact words of a speaker:
President Bush said, "We will not tire, we will not falter, and we will not
fail."

subject: English_grammar
text:
2. For a speech within a speech, the other style is used as inner quotation
marks:
‘Dave said, "Good afternoon, Frank" , recalled Frank.
Warning: Place the punctuation marks outside quotation marks, unless they
are logical parts of the quotation.
English Grammar and Composition 135
His answer to this was "no"; but two years later, he changed his mind.
Did he say "yes" or "no"?
